declared.title: Synthesizing the effects of mental simulation on behavior change: Systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « mental simulation process outcome meta-analysis » (2026-11-23)

population: 123 effect sizes from 94 studies (N = 5,685) of mental simulation against control; mean age 25, students in 78% of studies

findings.text: Mentally simulating a future behaviour improved that behaviour compared with control conditions

support.sentence: After applying a multilevel random effects model, a statistically-reliable positive effect of Hedges' g = 0.49, 95% CI [0.37; 0.62] was found, which was significantly different than zero.

findings.text: Picturing a successful outcome improved later behaviour a little compared with no simulation (15 effect sizes; 12 of them measured 1 to 19 weeks later)

support.sentence: However, it is important to state that the effect of superior outcome simulations (Hedges’s g = .23) was smaller than effects found for other subtypes—possibly because the effect of positive simulations are moderated by factors such as personality type and imagery content (Vasque & Buehler, 2007 ) or because these simulations are by nature less effective.
support.readBy: choose-your-struggle reviser, 2026-11-26: Europe PMC full text PMC8500882, Table 3, Discussion; data file ESM 2

findings.text: Rehearsing the steps alone (5 effect sizes) had a small effect compared with control that was not statistically significant

support.sentence: In the present meta-analysis, when participants focused upon instrumental plans toward one’s goal, rather than goal outcomes—the means rather than the end—there was a small positive effect that did not reach statistical significance within our multilevel moderation model.
support.readBy: choose-your-struggle reviser, 2026-11-26: Europe PMC full text PMC8500882, Discussion (footnote mark 6 left out)

findings.text: The effects of the different kinds of simulation (process, outcome, performance, combined) did not differ significantly from one another

support.sentence: While some subtypes appear to have different effects than others, an omnibus test of moderators shows that the effects are not statistically significantly different between subtypes of mental simulation, QM( df = 7) = 10.47, p = .1636.

limits: the omnibus test of subtypes was not significant (p = .16): subtype estimates are exploratory, some on very few studies (process: 5)
each subtype is compared with control, never process against outcome head to head; in the 4 studies with both arms, process did no better (ESM 2)
the 15 outcome effects: 12 in health, 10 with incentives, none from Oettingen's paradigm (idealized against questioning fantasies)
Pham 1999 is coded g = 0 for both its process and its outcome arm against control (exam, p < .09)
the Results text lists process among significant subtypes, against Table 3 (p = .20) and the Discussion: Table 3 is followed
students in 78% of studies; 59% of comparisons measured the same day; protocol not preregistered
countries not listed; no sample from the Middle East or North Africa known
